QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_50

question.text: Under SAS-1100, the SIA found that 875 families with damaged houses were EXCLUDED from Niwas because they lived in illegal structures (Chapter 8 finding). The SIA should:

answer.text: Recommend the SE abandon the programme
Disclose the exclusion as a 'Gap/Challenge' in Section III of the Report, noting the equity implication that the most vulnerable were excluded due to documentation status

explanation.text: The Logic: The Niwas case explicitly lists this as a Gap in Section III. Honest disclosure of exclusion patterns is a core SAS-1100 transparency requirement. It informs future programme design and equity-impact assessment. The Trap: Option A is concealment. Option C is prejudicial. Option B is disproportionate. Cross-Exam Context: Exclusion-equity analysis also in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — client-segmentation bias) and III-A / III-C (Compliance). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Draft a standing 'excluded-population table' for every SAS-1100 engagement: categories excluded, count, reason, equity implication. This is exactly what the Chapter 8 Niwas report does.
